assertions.name: A_reaches_30_digits_from_current_ck
assertions.source: A is the k→∞ limit of c_k·u^k sampled at k=8,9,10 only. Default expectation: 3 canonical rungs cannot pin A to 30 digits; the limiter is asymptotic convergence, not precision.

assertions.name: spread_is_intrinsic_not_compute_noise
assertions.source: Tail spread stable as compute dps rises 50→120 ⇒ intrinsic asymptotic spread, confirming compute precision is not the limiter.

description: Precision-ceiling analysis of residue A = lim_k c_k·u_subst^k (PR #1727 Step 1). A is the asymptotic limit sampled at k=8,9,10 (spread 0.0001955); the c_k are 50 dps so the limiter is asymptotic convergence, NOT arithmetic precision (spread stable across dps=True). Extrapolation (raw mean, Aitken Δ², 3-pt geometric) gives L ≈ 2.1177442455149e-13 (residue A = u_subst·L ≈ 1.8037324e-15) reliable to ≈ 4.02 sig figs (estimator spread 9.467e-5). ≥30 digits: False; ≥15: False. Genuine unblock = canonical c_11..c_15 extraction (NOT an ansatz fit). Diagnostic-only.

data.note_A_vs_L: L = lim c_k·u^k ≈ 2.118e-13 (tail limit); residue A = u_subst·L ≈ 1.804e-15 (canonical). u_subst exact ⇒ A and L share the same relative precision / achievable_digits.
data.genuine_unblock_path: Canonical (proved/near-match) extraction of c_11..c_15, extending the c_2..c_10 ladder — NOT an ansatz fit. With more rungs the asymptote tightens and extrapolation reaches grade.
